destination.title: Ready
destination.why: When the invitations come, you accept, because you genuinely feel you could pull it off.
destination.order: Work each capability's rungs in order. When capabilities compete for time: Algorithms, C++, the pricer, Performance, Concurrency, Probability, then Software design and Systems.

do: Wake at the same time. Every day, no exceptions.
One focus block on a live step. When two compete, the higher one wins.
Train: {training}. Then ten minutes of mobility.
Two problems into the solve log.
Money Stuff, and a little news.
The phone charges outside the bedroom. No screens in the final hour.
Read before bed, ten minutes at least.
Seven and a half hours in bed, at least.

protocol.never: No drinking, no smoking, no gooning, no dooming, no scrolling.
never_how: Zero, not less. Zero needs no decision.
Remove the access. Don't resist the urge.

week.text: The Sunday sync: count the week, set the next.

month: Takeaway two or three times, no more.

split.Mon: Lower A, squat focus, plus a finisher
split.Tue: Upper A, horizontal push and pull, plus a finisher
split.Thu: Lower B, hinge focus, plus a finisher
split.Fri: Upper B, vertical push and pull, plus a finisher
split.Sun: Arms, wrists, forearms and grip, twice a month

rules: Main lift 4 sets of 4 to 6 at RPE 7 to 8. Accessories 3 sets of 8 to 12 at RPE 8. Hit the top of the range on every set, then add weight next session.
Finishers: 8 to 10 minutes, after lifting. Carries and rower on upper days, bike or sled on lower days.
Tibialis raises and the single-leg calf eccentric in every lower session.
Ten minutes of mobility after every session: front rack, thoracic, ankles.
Wednesday VO2: 4 × 4 minutes at 180–190 bpm, 3 minutes easy between, 10 minutes warm-up, 5 minutes cool-down. Don't stack fatigue into it on Tuesday.
Deload every sixth week: same sessions, 60% of the weight, full reps.

stack.what: L-tyrosine 2000 mg, L-theanine 200 mg, then coffee in the same window.

stack.when: With the smoothie, about 30 minutes later
stack.what: Creatine 3–5 g, D3 + K2, B12 (methylcobalamin), benfotiamine 150–300 mg, zinc picolinate 15 mg.
150 ml unsweetened oat milk, 80 g 2% Greek yogurt, 100 g frozen berries, 50 g frozen banana, 10 g ground flax, 30 g protein powder.

recovery: A missed day costs one day. It costs the plan nothing. You return the next morning at the same wake time.
No debt, no catch-up. Nothing carries between days.
No replanning. Setting what this week should prove is fine. Rebuilding the roadmap isn't.

cadence.label: Every day
cadence.text: Two problems: the first from the current rung's set, the second from the NeetCode sections beside it. Until a rung's set opens, both come from NeetCode.

cadence.label: Fortnightly, from rung 2
cadence.text: A virtual Codeforces Div 3 round, two hours, no aids.

rungs.title: Analysis
study: Kleinberg & Tardos, Algorithm Design: Ch 5, divide and conquer
practise: Thirty recurrences by hand: substitution, recursion tree, master theorem
daily: NeetCode: Arrays and Hashing, Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Stack, Binary Search

rungs.title: Paradigms
study: Erickson, Algorithms: Ch 2, backtracking
Erickson Ch 4, greedy
Erickson Ch 3, dynamic programming, with its exercises
daily: CSES Dynamic Programming, once Ch 3 is read
Then the AtCoder Educational DP Contest
Then unseen Codeforces dp or greedy, most solved first: at 1400, then 1700
NeetCode: Backtracking, Greedy, Intervals, 1-D and 2-D Dynamic Programming

rungs.title: Containers, from scratch
study: At the hash map: the chapter of Celis's Robin Hood Hashing thesis that defines the scheme
Then Abseil's Swiss Tables notes, and Kulukundis's CppCon 2017 talk
practise: byo::hash_map against absl::flat_hash_map, on the same adversarial inputs
build: byo::vector, with amortised O(1) push
byo::list, with correct iterator invalidation
byo::deque, segmented
byo::stack, byo::queue, byo::priority_queue
byo::bitset
byo::hash_map: chaining, then Robin Hood, against adversarial hash inputs
Introsort (median-of-three quicksort, heapsort fallback, insertion sort finish) against std::sort
daily: Then unseen Codeforces at 1400–1700, any tag
NeetCode: Linked List, Heap / Priority Queue, Trees, Tries

rungs.title: Graphs
study: Erickson Ch 5–8: graph basics, depth-first search, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths
build: byo::graph: adjacency lists, one iterator for directed and undirected
byo::disjoint_set
On them: BFS, iterative DFS, Dijkstra on byo::priority_queue, Bellman–Ford, topological sort, Kruskal, Prim
daily: CSES Graph Algorithms, from the start through Road Construction
NeetCode: Graphs, Advanced Graphs, Math and Geometry, Bit Manipulation

rungs.title: Fluency
daily: Both problems: unseen Codeforces at 1700, any tag

rungs.title: Value semantics, ownership and the object model
study: Meyers, Effective C++, 3rd ed: Items 5–25 and 32–40
Sutter, Exceptional C++: the exception-safety and class-design items
Josuttis, C++ Move Semantics – The Complete Guide
Meyers, Effective Modern C++: Items 14 and 17–30, after Josuttis
Godbolt's talk, What Has My Compiler Done for Me Lately?
practise: The pricer's per-path loop in Compiler Explorer, x86-64 and ARM64, every instruction accounted for

rungs.title: Generic code and lambdas
study: Effective Modern C++: Items 1–4, type deduction
C++ Templates: The Complete Guide, 2nd ed: Ch 1–2 and 5, then traits, tag dispatch and enable_if
Josuttis, C++17 – The Complete Guide: if constexpr, CTAD, fold expressions
Josuttis, C++20 – The Complete Guide: concepts
Effective Modern C++: Items 31–34, lambdas, with what C++14, 17 and 20 added
build: The pricer core's requirement on its scalar type, written three ways: C++03 traits, C++11 SFINAE, C++20 concepts
Compared in Compiler Explorer

rungs.title: The rest of modern C++
study: Effective Modern C++: Items 5–13 and 15–16
From the Josuttis guides: optional, variant, string_view, structured bindings
The spaceship operator; ranges and views
consteval and constinit; designated initialisers
Coroutines and modules, skimmed

rungs.title: How the standard library does it
study: libc++, one question each:
vector: how reallocation stays exception-safe when elements move
shared_ptr: the control block, and why make_shared is one allocation
function: type erasure and the small-buffer optimisation
sort: where introsort's thresholds sit, and why

cadence.label: Design, from the first line
items: Core templated on scalar type
Exactly one type-erased boundary, at the factory rim
The per-path loop fully static and inlined
A new product is one new file, with zero core edits

rungs.title: Validation harness
study: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives: Wiener Processes and Itô's Lemma; The Black–Scholes–Merton Model
Skim Hull's Properties of Stock Options and Binomial Trees
Overton, Numerical Computing with IEEE Floating Point Arithmetic, 2nd ed: all but the hardware and language chapters
build: Closed-form Black–Scholes, separate from the Monte Carlo path
A standard error on every price
A tolerance between the two

rungs.title: Three seams
study: Joshi, C++ Design Patterns and Derivatives Pricing: Ch 1–9
build: Product, model and RNG, each varying without touching the others
European, digital, Asian and barrier products
Then lock the naive baseline, with machine, compiler flags and turbo state recorded

rungs.title: Floating point along a path
study: Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms: Ch 4, summation
build: mc754-paths, published: how rounding along a path moves the Asian and barrier prices
Naive against pairwise against Kahan
What each -ffast-math sub-flag breaks

rungs.title: Variance reduction
study: Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering: Ch 4, antithetic and control variates
build: Both, added through the seams
Measured as RMSE at fixed wall-clock time, against the baseline

cadence.label: Alongside
cadence.text: Muratori, Performance-Aware Programming: a section a week, in course order.

rungs.title: The instruments
study: Bakhvalov, Performance Analysis and Tuning on Modern CPUs: Part 1, Ch 1–6
Slotin, Algorithms for Modern Hardware: the RAM-model and cache-hierarchy articles
Berger's talk, Performance Matters
practise: The pricer's per-path loop profiled on both machines
perf on the 9800X3D, which needs Linux

rungs.title: The instruction level and the pipeline
study: Bryant & O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective: Ch 3
CS:APP Ch 4 §4.3–4.5, the sequential and pipelined processors
CS:APP Ch 5
Carruth's talk, Understanding Compiler Optimization
build: The bomb lab

rungs.title: The memory hierarchy
study: CS:APP Ch 6
Drepper, What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory: §3
Acton's talk, Data-Oriented Design and C++
build: The pricer's path storage switched between array-of-structs and struct-of-arrays
Measured on both machines

rungs.title: Vectorisation
study: Fog, Optimizing Software in C++: §12
build: vectranscend, published: the per-path loop vectorised, exp and log included
Accuracy against throughput

rungs.title: Correctness
study: Williams, C++ Concurrency in Action, 2nd ed: Ch 3–4 skimmed, then Ch 5

rungs.title: Memory consistency and orderings
study: Sorin, Hill & Wood, A Primer on Memory Consistency and Cache Coherence: Ch 1–5
Sutter's talk, atomic<> Weapons, both parts
Preshing's articles on memory ordering

rungs.title: The queue
study: Williams Ch 6–7
build: A single-producer single-consumer queue: mutex-based first, then lock-free
Bounded, no allocation after construction, wait-free on both sides
Head and tail on separate cache lines; clean under ThreadSanitizer
Benchmarked against each other with variance, and with the padding removed
Every memory ordering justified

rungs.title: Foundations
study: Blitzstein & Hwang, Introduction to Probability: Ch 1–4, with the Harvard Stat 110 lectures

rungs.title: The rest of the book
study: Blitzstein & Hwang Ch 5, 7 and 9: continuous distributions, joint distributions, conditional expectation
Skim Ch 6, 8 and 10
practise: Mosteller, Fifty Challenging Problems in Probability, in order
Then the probability chapters of Winkler, Mathematical Puzzles

rungs.title: Games and puzzles
practise: Chen & Ankenman, The Mathematics of Poker: Part I and the toy games
Crack, Heard on the Street: the quantitative sections

cadence.label: Microapplications
items: A few a week, in your list's order
Read the initial spec only; implement in 15–20 minutes
Then extensions in 10–15, 15–20 and 20–25 minutes
No AI

rungs.title: The small scale
study: Kernighan & Pike, The Practice of Programming, in dead time

rungs.title: The module scale
study: Ousterhout, A Philosophy of Software Design, in dead time

rungs.title: The machine and the OS
study: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces: Ch 13–20, virtual memory and allocation
OSTEP Ch 7–10, scheduling
Bonwick, The Slab Allocator, and tcmalloc's design document
build: A fixed-size pool allocator, plugged into byo::list's nodes
Benchmarked against the default allocator

rungs.title: The network path
study: Beej's Guide to Network Programming
Stevens, TCP/IP Illustrated Vol 1: TCP connection management and data flow

rungs.title: Market structure
study: Harris, Trading and Exchanges: Ch 1–6
CME's match-algorithm and MDP 3.0 market-data documentation
NYSE Pillar's order types and priority rules
The LMAX Disruptor paper
build: A limit order book on the byo containers
Price-time priority; add, cancel and modify; constant-time cancel

later.name: Phase 2 — Depth
later.note: Begins when Phase 1 closes, and is detailed then. Each capability continues where its Phase 1 rungs end.

parts.label: Algorithms
items: The rest of the byo library, in dependency order: treap, skip list, pairing heap
Sparse table, Fenwick tree, lazy and persistent segment trees
Heavy-light and centroid decomposition; modular arithmetic and FFT
Trie, suffix array, Aho–Corasick; flows
Codeforces 1500–2100, with the constructive and interactive tags

parts.label: C++
items: Effective Modern C++ Items 35–40
C++ Templates Ch 21
Alexandrescu, Modern C++ Design
Sutter, More Exceptional C++

parts.label: The pricer
items: Quasi-Monte Carlo: Sobol and Brownian bridge
Reverse-mode AAD, from Savine, Modern Computational Finance
The desk layer: implied vol solver, bootstrapped curve, fitted surface
QuantLib traced against the pricer; isbetray
At scale: a thread pool and per-thread tapes, scaling efficiency, the roofline

parts.label: Performance
items: Out-of-order execution in depth: Hennessy & Patterson, Computer Architecture, Ch 3
Throughput predicted with llvm-mca and uiCA, then measured
The roofline; LTO and PGO
Overton's hardware and language chapters, and the cost of denormals

parts.label: Concurrency
items: Litmus tests under herd7 and litmus7, on both machines
False sharing found from performance counters: linecache-false
Memory reclamation: Herlihy & Shavit, The Art of Multiprocessor Programming, and the hazard-pointer and epoch papers

parts.label: Probability
items: Chen & Ankenman beyond the toy games
Dixit & Nalebuff, Thinking Strategically

parts.label: Software design
items: Lakos, Large-Scale C++ Software Design
Functional Programming in Scala, Parts 1 and 3
The remaining microapplications

parts.label: Systems
items: The SPSC queue's latency distribution under isolcpus, IRQ affinity and transparent huge pages, with bpftrace
io_uring

parts.label: Mathematics, new
items: Velleman, How to Prove It
Spivak, Calculus, with Strang's Introduction to Linear Algebra and MIT 18.06
Hubbard & Hubbard, Vector Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Differential Forms

parts.label: The Analytics Engine
items: A columnar market-analytics engine in C++, from the wire up
The Systems order book grown into a matching engine inside it
The pool allocator and SPSC queue reused
Latency measured as p50, p99 and p999 against a locked baseline

parts.label: Mathematics
items: Abbott, Understanding Analysis, with Capiński & Kopp, Measure, Integral and Probability
Then Øksendal, Stochastic Differential Equations, Ch 1–6
